title: Recursion via the Z Combinator
description: Use the Z combinator to build recursive factorial and Fibonacci functions from non-recursive step lambdas.

steps.description: Define the applicative-order fixed-point combinator Z = lambda f: (lambda x: f(lambda v: x(x)(v)))(lambda x: f(lambda v: x(x)(v))).
Write step as a non-recursive lambda taking self and n, apply Z(step) to build factorial, and print the first eight factorials.

steps.question: In fib_step on line 11, what function is bound to self when fib = Z(fib_step) runs?
steps.answer: Z binds self to lambda v: x(x)(v), which unfolds fib_step again whenever self(n-1) or self(n-2) is called.

steps.description: Apply Z to fib_step to construct fib and print the first ten Fibonacci numbers.
Run line 8 to see Z(step) compute [1, 1, 2, 6, 24, 120, 720, 5040].
